**5. @Dpw_Jules**  
In the agentic economy, AI agents aren’t the only thing that needs to move fast. Trust does too.  

AI agents can already interact with tools, make decisions, communicate with other agents, and operate across environments.  

But one question still matters: Who stands behind the agent?  

That’s where @Concordium takes a different approach. Its Agent Registry creates an on-chain record for an agent and links ownership to an identity-verified Concordium account. That gives counterparties something they can check.  

🔐 Verified agent ownership  
🌐 Verification across Concordium, Ethereum, Solana and more  
👤 A link to a verified human or entity  
🔑 External agent keys can be linked to a Concordium account  
🛡️ Zero-knowledge proofs help verify credentials without exposing personal data  

The agent doesn’t have to move to Concordium. It can keep running on Google Cloud, Ethereum, Solana or elsewhere while carrying a verifiable accountability signal through the Concordium Agent Registry.  

The latest Concordium article highlights an important distinction with Google Agent Identity. Google’s system gives supported agents a cryptographic identity inside its runtime, helping answer “Which agent is running?”  

But when that agent interacts with an outside party, another question becomes important: “Who stands behind it?”  

Concordium’s Agent Registry is designed to address that cross-party accountability gap. A registry lookup can show that an agent record exists, whether it is active or revoked, which identity backed account owns it and its associated metadata and external keys.  

It does not prove the agent is honest, safe, or authorized for a particular transaction. That’s an important distinction.  

Identity isn’t the same as reputation. Registration isn’t the same as authorization.  

But a verifiable route back to the responsible party is a crucial foundation for trust between autonomous agents and the people or businesses they interact with.  

As AI agents become more autonomous, knowing what an agent can do is only part of the equation. Knowing who stands behind it matters too.  

Verified Humans.  
Verified Agents.  
One Protocol.  

$CCD

The real challenge with agentic payments isn’t simply allowing an AI agent to hold and spend funds.  

It’s making sure the agent can pay autonomously without being able to spend beyond the rules you set.  

That’s where Concordium becomes interesting.  

🔹 Protocol-Level Locks can define spending boundaries directly at the protocol level.  

🔹 Sponsored transactions can reduce the friction of transaction fees.  

🔹 x402 can enable AI agents to interact with services that require payments.  

Put these pieces together, and you get a much more practical model for agentic commerce:  

Discover → Decide → Pay → Settle  

All while keeping transactions within predefined rules.  

The future of AI payments isn’t just about giving agents access to money.  

It’s about giving them controlled financial autonomy.  

That’s the kind of infrastructure an agent economy needs.  

#ConcordiumAmbassador
